key_insight: A bilevel Late Acceptance Hill Climbing (b-LAHC) separates routing and charging decisions and introduces a surrogate upper-level objective to steer the search, accelerating convergence and improving solution quality for the Electric Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (E-CVRP).
problem_solved: Addresses the coupled, large-scale combinatorial challenge of jointly optimizing vehicle routes and charging schedules for electric fleets, where direct joint search is costly and prone to poor local optima.
method: Bilevel framework: upper level guides routing with a surrogate objective while the lower level evaluates/refines charging feasibility and energy constraints.

b-LAHC metaheuristic: a Late Acceptance Hill Climbing algorithm operating in three phases—greedy descent, neighborhood exploration, and bilevel joint refinement—to escape local minima and accelerate search.
Surrogate objective design to capture routing–charging interaction approximately, enabling faster evaluations and more effective guidance of the search.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable metaheuristic for EV routing that reduces search time and yields higher-quality feasible solutions; useful for AI/ML practitioners building real-world route-planning or hybrid optimization systems where evaluation cost and constraint coupling are bottlenecks.
visual_elements: Bilevel diagram showing upper-level routing (surrogate objective) and lower-level charging feasibility loop

Map-style illustration of routes with charging stops highlighted to show practical solution structure
paper_title: Bilevel Late Acceptance Hill Climbing for the Electric Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
paper_authors: Yinghao Qin, Mosab Bazargani, Edmund K. Burke, Carlos A. Coello Coello, Zhongmin Song
